answer: Because the jetty index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the raven audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the plume identifier and voids the later submissions, thus the operator pays for 74 runs and collects one. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 74 answers need 74 separate inference runs with separate seeds. That is 40 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
